header: IN THE HIGH COURT OF SINDH BENCH AT SUKKUR
HEARING ORDER WITH SIGNATURE OF HON’BLE JUDGE.
Respondent No.1 Abdul Razzak present, in person.
Mr. Niaz Hussain Maitlo, has filed Vakalatnama and statement
dated 23.11.2026 alongwith Special Power of Attorney that Abdul Razzak
son of Abdul Sattar Jamro, present Respondent No.1 is Attorney of
remaining Private Respondents who have preferred the Civil Appeal
No.09 of 2020, in which the impugned Judgment is passed. The
Advocate has opposed this Suo Moto reference and contends that the
Appellate Court Judgment is correct. Whereas learned Additional
Advocate General Mr. Ali Raza Balouch has submitted written
body: submissions and supported the Suo Moto reference and opposed the impugned Judgment. Has placed on record the Division Bench Judgment of this Court handed down in Constitutional Petition No.D-2009 of 2016, upholding the Suo Moto jurisdiction envisaged in Section 115 of the CPC. Further contends that Rule 23-A of Order XLI of CPC, as relied upon by the learned Appellate Court in its impugned Judgment, for remanding the LIS to the Trial Court, is not applicable in the Province of Sindh. Heard the learned counsel and the Law Officer.

Paragraph-32 of the impugned Appellate Judgment states that the Trial Court will decide the matter afresh on the basis of existing record. If the entire record is available then under Rule 24 of Order XLI of CPC the judgment is to be handed down by the Appellate Court. In this regard the justification offered in the Comments filed by the learned Presiding Officer is not plausible.

The Appellate Courts have to realize, that remanding the matters on trivial issues burden the ordinary litigants, besides adding-up to the backlog of the Trial Courts. Consequently, this Civil Reference is answered in affirmative that the impugned Appellate judgment is erroneous. It is set-aside. The Appeal filed by the Appellants shall be heard afresh and be decided within four weeks. R&Ps should be returned to the Trial Court.
J U D G E Ihsan/PS.
